units.title: Acute CHF Pathophysiology and IV Management
units.sec: Acute CHF Pathophysiology and IV Management · p77
units.guide: Acute CHF is most commonly caused by myocardial infarction. Acute myocardial injury decreases contraction, causes blood stasis in the heart, raises back pressure into the lungs, engorges pulmonary capillaries and extravasates plasma into parenchyma, producing pulmonary edema. Clinically the patient has chest pain and breathlessness; IV treatment of choice is dobutamine plus furosemide.

units.title: Acute CHF Inotropes and Pulmonary Edema Drugs
units.sec: Acute CHF Inotropes and Pulmonary Edema Drugs · p77
units.guide: Acute CHF management combines drugs that increase contraction and drugs that quickly relieve pulmonary edema. Dobutamine stimulates β1-Gs to raise cAMP and contractility without affecting heart rate; PDE3 inhibitors raise cAMP as inodilators; levosimendan opens K+ channels and sensitizes myocardium to Ca2+. Furosemide venodilates via prostaglandins and diureses; if there is no response, nitroglycerin and then nesiritide can be considered.

units.title: Chronic CHF Compensation, Mortality and Oral Drug Classes
units.sec: Chronic CHF Compensation, Mortality and Oral Drug Classes · p78
units.guide: Chronic CHF follows gradual loss of output from cardiomyopathy/rheumatic disease, then compensatory catecholamines and RAAS. Compensation may maintain output but drives cardiac remodeling, oxygen demand and mortality; decompensation resembles acute CHF and lowers oxygen supply. Oral mortality-reducing drugs target β1 signaling, heart rate, vasodilation, RAAS and sodium/water retention, while furosemide and digoxin remain symptomatic drugs.

units.title: Newly Diagnosed CHF Approach and Neprilysin/Guanylate Cyclase Drugs
units.sec: Newly Diagnosed CHF Approach and Neprilysin/Guanylate Cyclase Drugs · p79
units.guide: A newly diagnosed CHF patient first receives furosemide for symptoms, then a mortality-reducing foundation: sacubitril+valsartan if affordable is preferred to ACEI/ARB, otherwise ACEI/ARB are started low and titrated. β blockers are started while ACEI/ARB are being increased, beginning at suboptimal dose to prevent decompensation. Sacubitril raises BNP by inhibiting neprilysin, vericiguat raises cGMP through guanylate cyclase, and omapatrilat is obsolete because dual NEP+ACE inhibition caused fatal angioedema.

units.title: Digoxin Pharmacokinetics and Therapeutic Concentrations
units.sec: Digoxin Pharmacokinetics and Therapeutic Concentrations · p79
units.guide: Digoxin comes from Digitalis lanata, has good oral absorption, a long 36-48 hour half-life and renal excretion. Digitalization takes 7-10 days, so therapeutic drug monitoring should begin after that to avoid false low values. The normal plasma range is 0.5-2.0 ng/mL, but the desired therapeutic range is 0.5-0.9 ng/mL; toxicity rises above 2.0 ng/mL and mortality in atrial fibrillation rises above 1.2 ng/mL.

units.title: Digoxin Cellular Mechanism and Ventricular Arrhythmias
units.sec: Digoxin Cellular Mechanism and Ventricular Arrhythmias · p80
units.guide: At the cellular level, digoxin blocks the Na+-K+ ATPase pump. This raises intracellular Na+, blocks the Na+-Ca2+ exchanger, raises intracellular Ca2+ and increases myocardial contraction; extracellular K+ competes with digoxin binding, while diuretic-induced hypokalemia leaves more ATPase available and precipitates toxicity. In ventricles, delayed closure of Ca2+ channels causes DADs, extrasystoles, bigeminy, trigeminy, VT and finally VF, where defibrillation should be avoided.

units.title: Digoxin Toxicity Treatment and Organ-Level Heart Effects
units.sec: Digoxin Toxicity Treatment and Organ-Level Heart Effects · p81
units.guide: Digoxin toxicity is treated according to rhythm: lidocaine or amiodarone for VT/VF, Digibind as the antidote, and no dialysis because distribution volume is high. At normal dose digoxin is parasympathomimetic with SA/AV nodal block but also raises atrial Ca2+, causing atrial tachycardia as the most specific arrhythmia; therapeutically it converts atrial flutter into atrial fibrillation, which is easier to control. At high dose it becomes sympathomimetic with increased heart rate and contraction.

units.title: Digoxin Adverse Effects, Contraindications and DIGOXIN Summary
units.sec: Digoxin Adverse Effects, Contraindications and DIGOXIN Summary · p81
units.guide: The classic toxicity cluster is summarized by DIGOXIN: dialysis not done/Digibind, increased K+, gynecomastia, ocular effects/xanthopsia, increased arrhythmias, nausea-vomiting and Na+-K+ ATPase blockade. Nausea/vomiting is both earliest and most common. Toxicity risk rises with hypercalcemia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, MI and renal failure; digoxin is also contraindicated in HOCM and WPW.
